title: Functions, quadratics and coordinate geometry
lines: This topic ties algebra to pictures. A function is a rule, a quadratic is a function whose graph is a parabola, and a line is a function with constant slope. Most questions need one formula and careful substitution.
## Function notation
- f(x) = 2x² − 3x + 1 is a rule: replace every x with what is in the brackets, using brackets yourself.
- f(g(x)) means apply g first, then f. In general f(g(x)) ≠ g(f(x)).
- f(a + 1) is not f(a) + 1, and f(2x) is not 2f(x). Substitute the whole expression.
> For f(x) = 2x² − 3x + 1, find f(−2) and f(a + 1).
> f(x) = x + 3 and g(x) = x². Find f(g(2)) and g(f(2)).
! Squaring a negative input: for f(x) = x², f(−3) = (−3)² = 9. Writing −3² = −9 is the most common slip.
## Custom operations
- The GRE invents symbols such as a ◆ b = a² − ab. Follow the definition exactly and work inside brackets first.
- A made-up operation need not be commutative: a ◆ b and b ◆ a can differ.
> a ◆ b = a² − ab. Find (3 ◆ 1) ◆ 2 and 1 ◆ 3.
> 1 ◆ 3 = 1 − 3 = −2, while 3 ◆ 1 = 6: the order matters.
## Quadratics and their roots
- Standard form: ax² + bx + c = 0. Get zero on one side before factoring.
- Factor when you can: find two numbers with product c and sum b (when a = 1).
- Quadratic formula: x = (−b ± √(b² − 4ac)) / (2a). The discriminant b² − 4ac is positive (two real roots), zero (one root) or negative (no real roots).
- Sum of roots = −b/a; product of roots = c/a. These often answer the question without solving.
> Solve x² − x − 12 = 0.
> Two numbers with product −12 and sum −1: −4 and 3. So (x − 4)(x + 3) = 0 and x = 4 or x = −3.
> Check: sum of roots 4 + (−3) = 1 = −b/a; product −12 = c/a.
> Solve 2x² + 3x − 4 = 0.
> It does not factor nicely. b² − 4ac = 9 + 32 = 41, so x = (−3 ± √41)/4, about 0.85 or −2.35.
! Never cancel x from x² = 3x; you lose x = 0. And a quadratic usually has two roots: in QC, check whether both are allowed.
## Slope and equations of lines
- Slope m = (y₂ − y₁)/(x₂ − x₁): rise over run. Positive slope rises to the right; negative slope falls; horizontal lines have slope 0; vertical lines have undefined slope.
- Slope-intercept form: y = mx + b, where b is the y-intercept. Point-slope form: y − y₁ = m(x − x₁).
- Parallel lines have equal slopes. Perpendicular lines have slopes that multiply to −1 (negative reciprocals).
- A point lies on a line exactly when its coordinates satisfy the equation.
> Find the line through (−1, 4) and (3, −4). Is (5, −8) on it?
> At x = 5: y = −10 + 2 = −8. Yes, (5, −8) is on the line.
> Find the line perpendicular to y = 2x + 1 through (4, 1).
## Intercepts
- x-intercept: set y = 0. y-intercept: set x = 0.
> The line 3x − 4y = 12 and the two axes enclose a triangle. Find its area.
> y = 0 gives x = 4; x = 0 gives y = −3.
> The legs are 4 and 3, so the area is (1/2)(4)(3) = 6.
! Lengths are positive even when an intercept is negative. Use |−3| = 3 for the leg.
## Distance and midpoint
- Distance between (x₁, y₁) and (x₂, y₂): √((x₂ − x₁)² + (y₂ − y₁)²). It is the Pythagorean theorem on the grid.
- Midpoint: ((x₁ + x₂)/2, (y₁ + y₂)/2).
> Find the distance and midpoint between (1, 2) and (7, 10).
> Differences 6 and 8, so the distance is √(36 + 64) = √100 = 10.
## Parabolas
- y = ax² + bx + c opens upward when a > 0 and downward when a < 0. The vertex is at x = −b/(2a), and the graph is symmetric about that vertical line.
- Vertex form y = a(x − h)² + k has vertex (h, k). The minimum (or maximum) value is k.
- The x-intercepts are the roots of ax² + bx + c = 0; the y-intercept is c.
> Describe y = x² − 4x − 5.
> Vertex at x = 4/2 = 2; y = 4 − 8 − 5 = −9, so the vertex is (2, −9) and the minimum value is −9.
> Vertex form: y = (x − 2)² − 9. Roots: (x − 5)(x + 1) = 0, so x-intercepts 5 and −1, which sit symmetrically 3 units either side of x = 2.
> y-intercept: −5.
## Reading graphs of functions
- f(3) is the height of the graph above x = 3. The solutions of f(x) = k are the x-values where the graph meets the horizontal line y = k.
- Shifts: f(x) + k moves the graph up k; f(x − h) moves it right h (note the sign); −f(x) reflects it in the x-axis.
> The graph of y = x² is shifted 3 units left and 2 units down. What is the new equation?
> Left 3 replaces x with x + 3; down 2 subtracts 2: y = (x + 3)² − 2, with vertex (−3, −2).
! f(x − 2) moves the graph 2 to the right, not left. Check with one point: the vertex of (x − 2)² is at x = 2.
! Coordinate figures may not be drawn to scale. Use the given coordinates and equations, not how steep a line looks.
## Shortcuts
- Plug in for functions with letters: if f(x) = 3x − 1 and the question asks for f(f(x)), test x = 1: f(1) = 2 and f(2) = 5, so the right choice gives 5 at x = 1 (9x − 4 does).
- Sketch: a quick drawing of points and lines catches sign errors in slope.
- Use the calculator for square roots in distance questions only when the answer choices are decimals.
